2610.07535.title: Disentangling Models from Personas in Heterogeneous LLM Simulations
2610.07535.paper_summary: Multi-agent simulations with large language models (LLMs) often operate networks of agents with a single base model. This overlooks the inter-model effects which may dominate engagement dynamics in real-world deployments. To show this, we simulate a heterogeneous social network powered by several different base models and show that the amount of engagement an agent receives depends more on its base model than on its assigned persona. The attraction or repulsion effects of a base model strengthen dramatically when more models are added in the mix, suggesting that networks dynamics may converge to base model effects at scale. To help explain this effect, we conduct a series of content-mediating analyses, showing the predictability of base models across contexts as well as the relationship between a model's lexical patterns and an engagement-maximizing style. In light of recent developments in mass multi-agent interaction, this work underscores the relevance of heterogeneous compositions in driving the outcomes of those networks
2610.07535.paper_summary_zh: 多代理模擬與大型語言模型（LLMs）通常運行具有單一基礎模型的代理網絡。這忽視了可能主導現實世界部署中互動動態的模型間效應。為了展示這一點，我們模擬了一個由幾個不同基礎模型驅動的異質社交網絡，並顯示代理所獲得的互動量更多地依賴於其基礎模型，而非其指定的角色。當更多模型被加入時，基礎模型的吸引或排斥效應會顯著增強，這表明網絡動態在大規模下可能會收斂到基礎模型效應。為了幫助解釋這一效應，我們進行了一系列內容中介分析，顯示基礎模型在不同情境下的可預測性，以及模型的詞彙模式與最大化互動風格之間的關係。鑒於近期在大規模多代理互動中的發展，這項工作強調了異質組合在推動這些網絡結果中的重要性。
2610.07535.author: Dani Roytburg et.al.
